# Regeneration batch (living list)

Changes that alter corpus content (AER, SEM or PROV digests) and are therefore applied **together, once**, followed
by a single regeneration of the affected corpora. Started 2026-10-11.

**Preconditions:** phase 11's PROV-only `derive` (so SEM/PROV changes regenerate from the stored AERs in minutes
instead of a ~6-hour re-import); the user's approval of the final list and of the regeneration itself (standing rule:
no corpus is regenerated without approval). When built, the implementer chooses the best approach for each item within
the recorded constraints, states the expected digest changes before applying, and records the outcome here.

**Approval status (2026-10-11):** the user approved items 1–12 below **for implementation** on branch `regen-batch`
(code, tests, version bumps and a stated digest-change prediction per item). The regeneration of any corpus is **not**
approved yet; it needs a separate yes after the user has seen the predictions.

## Item 16 (implemented 2026-10-13, user-approved with the fetch extension; revised 2026-10-12 after the Inspect fetch; phase 10f F3, D-155): Inspect message copies, tool-event message ids, and the react `submit` result (WhistleBench)

**Evidence.** The user approved fetching the producer code (2026-10-12): `UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai` tags `0.3.130`
(`de88fe0b`) and `0.3.133`/`0.3.134`, blobless, depth 150, at `$AGENTPROV_HOME/upstream/github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai.git`
(logged in `acquisitions.jsonl`). The WhistleBench harness actors record `inspect_ai` `0.3.130` (8,050 samples) and
`0.3.134.dev31+geb46eef8` (1,150); `eb46eef8` is exactly 31 commits after tag `0.3.133` and an ancestor of `0.3.134`, so
both producer commits are pinned. The code cited below is the same at both (between them `_react.py` changes only in
typing, `_model.py` only in hooks and cache-usage reporting). WhistleBench itself (`legobridge/whistlebench@9c27637`, the
profile's pin, cached in staging) calls `react(name="Agent", submit=AgentSubmit(name="Submit", ...))`
(`highagency/whistlebench/tasks.py` l. 74-87; snitchbench uses the default name `submit`), with `keep_in_messages` at its
default `False` (`agent/_types.py` l. 127). Every count below is from the scratch corpus, read through the AERs and the
stored sample bytes (strict JSON loader), counts only.

**(a) One message, several stored forms: explained by code, so class D.** Every copy is a pydantic `model_copy`, which
keeps the message `id` and its `tool_calls`; only `content` (and, for submit, `tool_calls`) changes:
- `_remove_submit_tool` (`agent/_react.py` l. 483-525, called at l. 292 once the agent completes) rewrites the assistant
  message in `messages` without the submit call and without its last `reasoning` item. Shape counts: 9,190 message-id
  groups whose output-choice copy holds a submit call that the `messages` copy lacks (2,909 of them also lose the
  reasoning item); every non-submit call identical across the copies.
- `resolve_reasoning_history` (`model/_model.py` l. 1146-1231 at `0.3.130`, l. 1164-1249 at `eb46eef8`, applied at
  l. 575/589 before the `ModelEvent` records `input`) drops or `<think>`-emulates reasoning in the history re-sent to
  the model. 2,836 groups: `messages` copy with reasoning, replayed `input` copy without.
- 0 groups whose non-submit calls differ. The 11 duplicates across different message ids stay ambiguous.

**(b) The tool event's `message_id` is the first result message of its batch: an Inspect defect, class D.** In
`execute_tools` (`model/_call_tools.py`), `result_messages` is created once per assistant message (l. 251), outside the
per-call loop (l. 253), and each `ToolEvent` gets `message_id=result_messages[0].id` (l. 321). So for the second and
later calls of a parallel batch, `message_id` names the *first* call's result message. Effects in the scratch corpus:
6,826 tool-result messages have no generating execution (the mapper links an execution to its result through
`message_id` and never overwrites a link, so no execution is linked to a wrong result, but the later results are
orphaned); 795 submit events "find" another tool's result message. AgentHarm (stored): 0 orphaned results, 4,148 links
all matching the answered call; nothing there moves.

*Range (phase 10h's measurement, relayed 2026-10-12; `~/.agentprov/migration-work/phase10h/scripts/parallel_calls.py`,
recorded there as R-H4):* fragfuse logs at `inspect_ai` `0.3.154.dev37+g1289c1ad` (802 parallel batches in 620 samples;
1,617 of 5,078 tool events name another call's result) and `0.3.159.dev20+g3ddd7997` (87 batches in 73 samples; 155 of
567) show the same defect, and those 693 samples are exactly the fragfuse trial's 693 `accounting_inconsistent`
(`aer.acc.executions_have_results@1`) samples; `0.3.158` had no parallel batches; kexin at `0.3.263` (1,551 batches) has
every present `message_id` agreeing with its call, so the defect is fixed by then. So it is observed from `0.3.130` to at
least `0.3.159.dev20`. The code is cited (D) at the two WhistleBench commits only; fragfuse's commits `1289c1ad` and
`3ddd7997` are not in the fetched history, so for them the fallback link is I unless the same fetch is extended to those
two commits (a separate yes).

**(c) The submit result is recorded in the tool event; only its message was removed.** All 9,201 submit tool events
carry `result` (a string; 56 empty). For 8,404 of them the result message is absent from `messages`, removed by
`_remove_submit_tool` (it drops every tool message of the submit function). The other 797 are the (b) cases. So the
item's earlier reading ("not recorded") is wrong: the value is observed; what is missing is the message, by the
harness's design.

**Proposal.**
1. *(a)* When every part holding a `ToolCall.id` belongs to messages of one Inspect message id and the calls are
   byte-identical, the call is one call: `call` and `responds_to` resolve to the copy the call was produced in (the
   model output choice, else the `messages` copy, never a replayed input). New rule
   `inspect.message_copies_share_calls@1`, **class D**, citing `_react.py` l. 483-525 and `_model.py`
   `resolve_reasoning_history` at both commits. Message records stay separate; no content is merged.
2. *(b)* A tool event's result message is found by `tool_call_id` equal to the event's `id` (the call id); `message_id`
   is used only where it agrees. The rule is version-independent in what it does (it trusts the call id, which every
   version writes correctly), so it applies to every Inspect profile; its class follows the citation policy (D where
   the producing commit's code is cited, otherwise an `_unverified` twin, I). New rule `inspect.tool_event_message_id_first_of_batch@1`, **class D**, citing
   `_call_tools.py` l. 251-321 at both commits, on the links made by the fallback. Where `message_id` agrees (every
   AgentHarm link, every first call of a batch), the existing citations stay, so AgentHarm's bytes do not move.
3. *(c)* For an execution of the profile's declared submit tool whose result message was removed: the result is mapped
   from the event's `result` as an artefact `generated_by` the execution (`inspect:tool_result`, located at
   `/events/<k>/result`, O), no result message is invented, and the absent message is declared, not raised as
   `missing_tool_result`/`dangling_source_ref`. New rule `inspect.react_submit_message_removed@1`, **class D**, citing
   `_react.py` l. 292 and 483-525 and WhistleBench `tasks.py` l. 74-87. Profile key: `[family.inspect]`
   `submit_tools = ["Submit", "submit"]` in `whistlebench.profile.toml`.

**Digest prediction.**
- **Stored corpora:** no AER changes (AgentHarm: 0 orphaned results, 0 call-link conflicts, its 4 missing results are
  not submit; the new rules fire nowhere there). The `inspect` catalogue and adapter code digests move, so the PROV of
  `ast-survey-agentharm` changes in its catalogue attribute only.
- **fragfuse** (phase 10h, scratch only; no fragfuse corpus exists outside scratch): AER bytes change in the 693
  affected samples; their `accounting_inconsistent` should clear. Measured on the 10h scratch import after
  implementation.
- **WhistleBench** (trial only, D-155): about 3,440 of 3,452 samples lose `call_result_link_conflict`; 6,826 orphaned
  results gain their generating execution; 8,404 `missing_tool_result`/`dangling_source_ref` pairs become declared
  removals with the result kept as an artefact; `accounting_inconsistent` falls with them. To be measured on the
  scratch corpus after implementation, before WhistleBench is imported.

**Rejected:** merging the copies (loses what the model was re-sent); matching by call id alone without the
same-message-id condition (hides the 11 genuine cross-message duplicates); trusting `message_id` (wrong for every later
call of a batch at these versions); inventing a result message for submit (the model never saw one); class I (the
behaviour is read from the pinned producer code at both versions).

**Implemented (2026-10-13, branch `claude/item-16-inspect`; D-155 addendum).** The user approved item 16 and the fetch
extension to fragfuse's commits: `1289c1ad` is 37 commits after tag 0.3.153 and `3ddd7997` 20 after 0.3.158 (fetched as
tags 0.3.153/0.3.154/0.3.158/0.3.159 into the same blobless store, logged). The cited code is the same at all four
producer commits, so all three rules are class D with `code` lists at each. Two refinements found while implementing:
- **(b) is narrowed to the defect's signature:** the call-id fallback applies only where `message_id` names a tool
  message that answers another call. A `message_id` naming no message stays unlinked with `missing_tool_result`
  (`test_mapping_rows.py::test_dangling_tool_message_gives_missing_tool_result` keeps its meaning), so AgentHarm's 16
  missing results are unchanged.
- **Declarations, not silence:** the core accounting counts a result only through a message's `generated_by` or a listed
  `missing_tool_result`, and a call part only through an execution, a denial or a listed `unexecuted_tool_call`
  (invariant 5: no core change). So the copies' parts are listed `unexecuted_tool_call` citing
  `inspect.message_copies_share_calls@1`, and a removed submit message is listed `missing_tool_result` citing
  `inspect.react_submit_message_removed@1`, with its value kept as the artefact. No `dangling_source_ref` for it.

Code: `adapters/inspect/mapper.py` (`_produced_copy`, `call_part`, `_tool_message`, `_submit_result`, the copy
declarations), `family.schema.json` (`submit_tools`), `whistlebench.profile.toml`, the catalogue (three rules and type
`inspect:tool_result`). Tests: `tests/adapters/inspect/test_item16.py` (5).

**Measured** (re-mapped from the stored member objects, old code = `origin/main` 733a78f, new = this branch):

## Item 28 ((i) implemented, 2026-10-13; user-approved; routed from phase 10n, R-10n-2): Inspect strings over 1 MiB

**Finding.** ATIA (phase 10n, inspect_ai 0.3.112) has 42 strings whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds 1 MiB:
- 20 image `data:` URIs and 4 video values in message parts;
- 18 Gemini `inlineData` copies in `model_call.params.transmitted`.

C.2.1(6) requires such a string to be stored as a blob and referenced. They pass validation today because the AER
validator and writer do not check C.2.1(6) (question (iii) below).

**Constraints** (deferrals session, 2026-10-13):
- `$blob` is a reserved Json form, valid in every Json position in aer/0.1 and unchanged in aer/0.2. That includes
  `model_call.params`, so `params.transmitted` qualifies.
- `$blob` is not valid in typed string fields: `parts[k].uri` and `text` are plain strings. Widening `uri` is outside
  what the user approved for aer/0.2.
- A `$blob` must name a raw-store object listed in `seal.blobs`. Imports store only whole raw files (D-203), so nothing
  can store a string carved out of a source JSON yet.

**(i) Proposed now (Inspect mapper; new rule `inspect.content_not_inlined@1`, class D; issue
`inspect.content_not_inlined`, severity info).** This follows the OpenHands precedent
(`openhands.content_not_inlined@1`, phase 10g).
- A `data:` URI over 1 MiB in a message part becomes a `blob` part (`{"t": "blob", "media": <the URI's media type>}`,
  C.3.4.1), with `/parts/k/data` declared `not_captured`.
  - The URI's digest and size go in `ext.inspect.part_extra[k].not_inlined`, as `{sha256, bytes, media}` of the URI
    string's UTF-8 bytes.
  - The locator names the source position.
  - With (ii), the same part later gains `data` as a `$blob` of the decoded payload. A plain URL over 1 MiB (none
    observed) would stay a `uri` part with `/parts/k/uri` declared `not_captured` and the same digest in ext.
- A string over 1 MiB in a Json position (`params.transmitted`, tool args, `other.value`) is replaced in place by
  `{"not_inlined": {sha256, bytes, media?}}`, the OpenHands form.
- Honest but lossy: the content stays in the raw store and out of the AER, and its digest ties it to the raw bytes.

**(ii) Separate decision (runner, raw origins, C.11.5; the deferrals session's capability): carved blobs.**
- The mapper returns the carved bytes with a locator into the source artefact.
- The runner stores them under a new origin kind, e.g. `{kind: "carved", from: <source sha256>, pointer}`.
- `verify` and `recompute` re-carve and compare.
- No AER schema change is needed. It would serve ATIA's 42 strings and OpenHands' not-inlined content alike. When it
  lands, (i)'s declarations become `$blob` references.

**(iii) Separate question (core, `aer/validate.py`): enforce C.2.1(6).**
- A release-mode check of string sizes would have caught these 42 strings.
- Scanned 2026-10-13: 0 lines over 1 MiB in the 126,747 AERs of the nine current stored corpora, so no stored AER would fail.
- It is a core change (invariant 5 record).

**Prediction for (i).**
- No stored AER byte: the scan above found no line over 1 MiB, so no stored string reaches the threshold.
- The `adapters/inspect` code and catalogue digests move.
- ATIA (not stored): 24 parts and 18 `params.transmitted` values are declared not inlined, and the AER shrinks by
  their size.

**Implemented (i), with one change of form.** aer/0.1 makes a `blob` part's `data` strictly required, and a declared
unknown may stand beside a value only as `ambiguous` (AER-V16). So a blob part "declared `not_captured`" and a null
`text` "declared `not_captured`" do not validate. Instead, every oversized string takes a Json position:
- an `image`, `audio`, `video`, `text` or `reasoning` item becomes `{"t": "other", "type": <the Inspect type>,
  "value": {"not_inlined": {sha256, bytes, media?}}}`, with the item's other fields in `part_extra` as before;
- a tool message's string content becomes the `tool_result`'s `value`;
- strings in Json positions (`params.configured`/`transmitted`, call `args`, `other` values, list-content results,
  events kept in `ext`) are replaced in place.

Every replacement is tagged D under `inspect.content_not_inlined@1` scoped to its pointer. One info issue,
`inspect.content_not_inlined`, lists the records. `media` comes from a `data:` URI. The threshold is C.2.1(6): UTF-8
bytes over 1 MiB, so exactly 1 MiB stays inline. With (ii), the `other` parts become `blob` parts with a `$blob`, and
the Json replacements become `$blob` references.

Checked:
- Re-mapped AER bodies are byte-identical to item 25's: AgentHarm 1,056 of 1,056, scratch WhistleBench 9,200 of 9,200.
- `tests/adapters/inspect/test_item28.py` (5): a data URI image; a tool output; text and reasoning items; a
  transmitted string; the exact-1-MiB boundary. Each case passes tier 4.

## Item 80 (implemented 2026-10-14; R-10p-7, routed from phase 10p; user-approved for the round; branch `r10p7-sandbox-output`): Inspect sandbox events without an output

**Status: lands on main alone** (user decision 2026-10-14, relayed by the orchestrator), ahead of the round, so that
phase 10p can seal. The `map` stage code digest moves for every Inspect corpus (`adapters/inspect/mapper.py`). The
corpora are re-derived in the regeneration round, and no stored AER, SEM or PROV bytes move.

**Defect.** `InspectEvalMapper._sandbox` emitted an `inspect:sandbox_output` artefact (`ev = "O"`, `by = "source"`) for
every top-level `sandbox` event. When the event holds no `output` string (`write_file`, or an `exec` whose output is
null) the artefact's only asserted fields are D (`/type`, `/generated_by`) and its content is `unk`. So the writer refuses
the record set (AER-V12 `by_without_bare_O`) and the runner seals the sample degenerate (`map.adapter_defect`,
`aer.write.invalid`). Phase 10p's trial t1 had 5,522 of 5,522 control-arena executions affected.

**Choice (this session's call, as routed).** No artefact when the event records no output string. An empty string
is still an output and keeps its artefact. The source records no generated entity, so none is claimed (invariant 2).

*Rejected:* keeping the artefact without `by = source` or bare-O evidence, which would be a placeholder entity with
unknown content that no field of the source attests.

The activity record (`inspect:sandbox_<action>`, status, `ext` fields, times) is unchanged. The catalogue rule
`inspect.sandbox_activity@1` ("whose output is an artefact") still holds, so there is no catalogue or profile change
and no bump. D.9 mapping row amended.

**Predicted.** The `map` stage code digest moves (`adapters/inspect/mapper.py`) for every Inspect corpus. No AER, SEM or
PROV bytes move in any stored corpus: the old path could only produce a refused record set, so any affected sample
was already degenerate, and stored Inspect corpora hold no `adapter_defect`. Control-arena (not stored; phase 10p) goes
from degenerate to mapped samples.

**Measured.**
- `ast-survey-agentharm-p10.partial`: 1,056 AERs, 0 sandbox activities, 0 `sandbox_output` artefacts, 0 `adapter_defect`.
  Byte-neutral.
- There is no stored whistlebench corpus.
- `tools/regen_pins.py --check`: every family is current.
- `tests/adapters/inspect/test_r10p7_sandbox.py`: 3 no-output cases fail on the old mapper and pass on the fix, and
  2 output cases pass on both.
- Phase 10p's strict xfail `test_a_sandbox_write_without_output_maps_to_valid_aer` (on `phase-10p-holds` bfd0e7d7)
  stays failing on the fix, for a second reason in its synthetic event: `completed=s.tick(0.1)` is evaluated before
  `event()` ticks the clock for the event's own timestamp, so the event ends before it starts (AER-V19
  `aer.order.time` `start_after_end`, `adapter_defect` again). With the times in order, the same event maps cleanly
  (the `write-null` case here). Phase 10p fixes its fixture and drops the marker.

  core-review-C stop flag lands). A true drain exits 0 with outcome `drained`. Until then a drain degrades to a stop
  (built).

  - The option: for `import`, `derive`, `recompute` and `run`. It is refused with `--release` (exit 2) and in the

## Item 101 (built 2026-10-15; D-455, R-10j-3; user decision 2026-10-15: approved; held branch `bugpass-regen-d455`)

URL download pins become archive inputs, as Zenodo and Hugging Face files are (D-200): `DOWNLOAD_PIN_KINDS` gains
`url`. The file is checked against the pinned SHA-256 and size, stored with a `url {url, retrieved}` origin, expanded in
place and its members mapped. A URL is mutable, so the retrieval time comes only from the recorded fetch: the fetch
cache's acquisition record (`FetchResult.retrieved_at`, also read back on a cache hit), else the pin's `retrieved_at`
(RFC 3339 UTC). With neither the import is refused (`raw.origin.unpinned`, exit 3); nothing is stamped with the time of
the import. The working snapshot `pin` records `retrieved_at`, and the seal builds `{kind: url, url, retrieved_at}`
(H.2.3). Re-maps label the stored object by its URL, then by the recorded input label.

| AER, SEM, PROV, validation, index, register, manifest | **none** for every existing corpus: no stored corpus has a `url` snapshot (the import refused them before) |
| `derivation.json` | `adapters/runner/` is in the `aer` stage's `engine_code_sha256`, so that digest and the stage's `fn_digest` move for every corpus imported or re-mapped afterwards |

## Item 145 (item-7 follow-up; found by artefact catalogues, routed by the orchestrator 2026-10-21; held branch `regen-held-2`): lone surrogates in digested text

- **Defect.** Three digests encoded source text strictly as UTF-8:
  - `agentdojo/mapper.py` `_prompt_variant`, the D.6.6 system-prompt variant digest;
  - `hooks/autodojo.py` `slot_cells`, the payload and wrapped-goal digests against the ROPE cache table.

  A lone UTF-16 surrogate, which the strict loader keeps (C.11.4, item 7), raised `UnicodeEncodeError`. The whole log
  then mapped as `adapter_defect`, a degenerate AER.
- **Fix.** Both encode with `surrogatepass`.
  - Valid text gives the same bytes and the same digest.
  - Text holding a lone surrogate matches no pinned variant or cache cell. For a prompt variant that gives the info
    issue `agentdojo.system_prompt_unrecognised`; for a payload slot, form `none`.
  - No rule or catalogue change.
- **Tests.** `tests/adapters/agentdojo/test_item145_surrogate_digests.py` (2). Both fail on the unfixed code.
- **Census.** The stored corpora hold 0 `adapter_defect` executions: agentdojo-upstream 2024-06 and head, agentdyn-a,
  ast-survey-agentdojo, mandate and rope, all p10, 148,631 executions in all. So no stored AER, SEM or PROV byte
  moves. The agentdojo adapter code digest moves.

## Item 133 (pre-check PC-04, control-arena; user decision 2026-10-21: split per scope; held branch `regen-held-5`): a cached scorer call's output is its scope's own message

- **Finding (10p t2, ids only).** In every one of the 910 several-result calls in 364 executions:
  - the second scorer's model call is a cache hit (`status cached`);
  - an activity in its scope re-runs the sandbox commands at its own times.

  The merge by Inspect message id made those results a second result of the first scorer's call. That gave
  `aer.acc.tool_results_linked@1` `call_has_several_results`, `map.accounting_inconsistent` and `known_incomplete`,
  though nothing is lost.
- **Choice.** The user first chose an expected-known quirk. Told that it leaves the executions `known_incomplete`,
  they chose to split per scope (2026-10-21). Rejected: linking the results as copies, an expected-known quirk, and a
  core accounting exemption.
- **Change (Inspect mapper only).**
  - `_register` gives a cache hit's output its own message when another scope produced the message.
  - Later holders in that scope, including pooled `input_refs`, resolve to that copy.
  - Its tool calls are indexed per scope (`split_calls`). `call_part` (tool events, approvals) and `_link_result`
    resolve them by scope.
  - New class D rule `inspect.cached_output_own_message@1` (`inspect_ai` `_model.py` at 0.3.130, 0.3.134.dev31,
    0.3.154.dev37 and 0.3.159.dev20). It is cited on the copy's `generated_by`, the result's `responds_to` and the
    tool execution's `call`.

### Item 108 (D-510 safeguard): the account-path lint at selection (D.2.9 item 17)

- `adapters/account_paths.py` recognises the account-directory shapes. The runner (`_hold_account_paths`, before the
  per-unit stage) holds a selected file as `select.redaction_pending` when no redaction pattern of its profile covers the
  shaped segment. The detail names the shape and segment index only. `[import] account_path_exempt` takes reviewed globs.
- **Measured.** No hit over the about 137k labels of the stored corpora, so no stored corpus changes. Over every staging
  clone, only EnvironmentOptim's 5,912 `munged_cluster` paths, which item 106's rule covers.
- **Test.** `tests/adapters/runner/test_account_path_lint.py`:
  - the shapes and exemptions;
  - an uncovered path is held under agentdojo-upstream;
  - an EnvironmentOptim arm maps as Qwen3.5-9B with no account in its AER;
  - a degenerate unit under a redacted arm holds no account.
- **Order fix (pre-round review #7, branch `integration-fix-108`).** The hold now runs after RD-3's `pin_candidates`
  snapshot. A listing pin covers the whole selected listing, so a held file that is missing from it would make every
  other file `raw.origin.blob_mismatch`. The held file is still registered and never imported. This was latent: only
  adprov-v1 has a listing pin, and no label of it is account-shaped. Test:
  `test_a_held_file_stays_in_the_listing_a_listing_pin_is_checked_against`, which fails before the fix. Prediction:
  the aer stage `engine_code_sha256` moves for every family (`adapters/runner` is in its D-451 scope), as with item
  108 itself. No stored byte moves.
- **Coverage fix (pre-round review #19, same branch).** `covered()` counted any pattern match anywhere in the
  account's segment as cover, and ignored a rule's `labels` allowlist. So D-607's dtap `host_account_token` (a match
  on every token) made the lint vacuous under dtap-bench@2. A rule now covers an account only when:
  - one of its matches in that segment includes the account token (its `span` group, else the whole match);
  - for a rule with `labels`, the span's `{span12}` label, salted with the profile id, is listed.

  `account_shapes` keeps the token in memory for this check only, never in a report or row. Tests: a match that misses
  the account, and a listed versus an unlisted label (and the wrong salt).
  - **Measured:** the only account-shaped labels in any staging clone are EnvironmentOptim's, and its rule still
    covers them. No file is newly held, and no stored byte moves. `account_paths.py` is outside the stage scopes, and
    the importer's one-argument change moves the aer engine digest only with the order fix above.

cap (N.1.7: resumed units do not consume it), so a different limit is allowed. This follows CLI robustness's reading in
its unused draft `e435967e`, whose limit test was ported. The snapshot records the cap as a running total of the units
it holds, so a re-map reproduces them.

  its 2 executions.

  This is plausible but not reproduced.
- Inherent: an interleaved `--limit` extension of one snapshot around another snapshot's import cannot be replayed
  exactly.

## Items 98–100 (D-530, D-560; session phase-10i follow-up; user-approved 2026-10-14/15; held branch `phase-10i-context`)

Write-up: `docs/reports/phase10i/D-530-archive-context-pin.md`. Trial evidence: `docs/reports/phase10i/README.md` §10.

- **Item 98: re-map with per-unit inputs** (`corpus/rawtree.py`, `corpus/derive.py`, one `import_source` hunk).
  - A re-map (`recompute`, `derive` of `expand`/`aer`, `verify --level rederive`) rebuilds the context trees and
    pinned objects a snapshot recorded.
  - `StoredRawTree` keeps context files and LFS objects out of the primary inputs. Without this, DTap's LFS pointer and
    its object collided on one label (`corpus.rawtree.invalid`).
- **Item 99: the CLI wires per-unit inputs** (`cli/import_.py`, runner hunks).
  - Declared context pins come from `--context ROLE=PATH` or the fetch cache; `--no-context ROLE` skips one.
  - A download pin is an archive context (RedCode Qwen Code's supplementary zip).
  - `lfs_object` pins give pinned objects, including for readers without per-unit inputs (MCPHunt).
- **Item 100: D-560.** Archive members that a profile `exclude` entry names are registered and counted in
  `selection_excluded`.

**What moves.**
- **`aer` stage `engine_code_sha256`** (`adapters/runner` + `aer`, class 1), on the pre-round integration premerge
  (2026-10-21): `sha256:6f85c964…63ed93a7` (integration head `2c69be39`) → `sha256:882fcbc7…3f1806`
  (`phase-10i-context-premerge`). Only `adapters/runner/importer.py` differs under those directories. Earlier predictions
  were `856b7a09…` → `10359560…` (against `0f668fdf`) and `7e71c65f…` → `be047ce3…` (against `da2e0252`). Any later commit
  to `adapters/runner/` or `aer/` on either side moves it again. It moves for every corpus at its next import or re-map.
- **No `expand` code digest moves.** A first build added `RawObjectStore.locate` to `raw/store.py`, which is an
  `EXPAND_MODULES` file, so it would have moved every archive corpus's `expand` digest. The premerge reads the stored
  object's path in `corpus/rawtree.py` instead (`StoredRawTree._locate`), and `raw/` is untouched. `cli/` and `corpus/`
  are in no stage digest.
- **One more `expand` stage definition** for each corpus with an archive context (none stored today).
- **Register rows and `selection_excluded` counts (D-560)** for archive-input corpora with `exclude` entries.
  AgentOps-Bench's import gains 3,842 `select.out_of_scope` rows and 4 `select.not_execution_artefact` patterns' worth
  of rollup rows. Others: `credleak-p15b`, `code-agent-misalignment-geminicli`, `seagent-agentdojo`,
  `controlarena-persistent`, and 10j's `authority-caps`/`ipi-defenses`. Their next import's `register.jsonl` and
  manifest counts differ by exactly those rows.
- **`snapshot.context[]`** gains `pin` (and `input` for an archive context) in working manifests built with a context
  tree. Sealed corpus-0.1 manifests carry no context entry.
- **`snapshot.context[].verification`** (pre-round review PR-1, 2026-10-22, class 2 for working manifests;
  user-approved in the deferrals window, D-221 addendum): a context tree the CLI resolves without a `PinCheck` records
  how it verified itself instead of `null`: `{kind: "download", verified: <stored>, unverified: 0}` for a download pin's
  archive (RedCode Qwen Code's and redcode-exec-openhands' `supp`), `{kind: "blob", ...}` for a git pin read from the
  fetch cache (DTap's and AgentOps-Bench's `tasks` with `--fetch`). A `--context ROLE=PATH` copy keeps its `PinCheck`
  counts (kind `blob`); a re-map carries the recorded value (NF-26). Without it, D-221's seal refused these
  corpora (`package.refused.unverified`).

**No AER, SEM or PROV byte changes for a corpus imported with its context.** A re-map now *restores* the joins that a
re-map used to drop. Before the change, the AgentOps-Bench trial showed 3,360 unexplained changes and DTap (no LFS) 40 of
48; with the change, `recompute --dry-run` is identical, which the regression tests check. DTap corpora with LFS objects
become re-mappable for the first time: their recompute gate never ran before.

**Expected after it lands.** `recompute` at main reports the `aer` stage digest drift for stored corpora (a
code-digest-only change). Archive-input corpora with excludes show the D-560 register rows as corpus-file differences
until they are re-imported in the round.

**What changes.**
- A run that stops before it ran to the end marks its snapshot `incomplete: {"reason": "drained" | "interrupted"}`
  and the corpus `partial`. `drained` is a D-394 drain; `interrupted` means `run` raised: a first SIGINT, SIGTERM or
  SIGHUP, `stop`, or any error. A drain that NF-36's cumulative cap describes (with a clean tail: its last mapped
  candidate ended in a counted unit) is not marked; an interrupt always is; an earlier mark is never hidden by a later
  cap (review amendment, NF pass, 2026-10-21).
- A later run of the snapshot that ran to the end with nothing left to map clears the mark. It must have mapped and
  had no `--limit`, or found fewer units than its limit.
- `package` refuses a marked corpus (`package.refused.incomplete`), and `derive`/`recompute` refuse it as their
  source (`corpus.derive.incomplete`). NF-36's caps are unchanged.

**What moves.** `adapters/runner/importer.py` is in the `aer` stage's code digest, so the `aer` `engine_code_sha256`
moves for imports made afterwards (class 1; item 130 moves the same digest; corpora imported before see it as code
drift, D-430). `corpus/runstate.py` (new), `corpus/package.py`, `corpus/derive.py` and `cli/import_.py` are class 0.

**No AER, SEM or PROV byte changes.** A corpus no run stopped carries no mark. Only a working manifest a stopped
run left gains the snapshot member.

**Tests.** `tests/adapters/runner/test_incomplete_mark.py`.

## Item 165 (post-round known issue; D-621 amendment 3; recorded 2026-10-22 on the orchestrator's ruling: not fixed before the round; built 2026-10-23 on the held branch `prov-item165-apv-note` together with the apv 0.2.0 note, one prov digest move by user decision 2026-10-22)

| # | Item | Source | Changes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 165 | Two carried-over, unchanged state changes (`apv:EnvironmentCarriedOver`) with the same cause both state `used(cause, predecessor state)` under `aprov.env_call@1`/`aprov.env_pass@1`, so `derive` refuses with `prov.statement_collision` (`prov/rules/edges.py` `_state_change`; found by the D-621 amendment 3 chain test). **Fix before any family adopts `apv:EnvironmentCarriedOver`** | DECISIONS D-621 amendment 3 | prov `engine_code_sha256` when fixed; no stored bytes, since no adapter catalogue declares the assumption | **Built 2026-10-23 (held, class 1).** Fails closed before the fix (a refusal, not a false tier-4 result) |

**The fix.** Each fact is stated once, citing every carried-over state change that supports it. `Ctx.rel(..., merge=True)`
adds a repeat (same rule, section, arguments, path, attributes and discriminator) to the first statement's fields and
citations. `_state_change` uses it for the carried-over `used` and `wasInvalidatedBy` only, so a chain whose first
carried link is unchanged and a fork with the same cause derive too. No relation is added. Rejected alternatives are in
D-621 amendment 3. Regression test:
`tests/unit/prov/test_tier4_bindings.py::test_carried_over_state_changes_with_one_cause_share_one_statement` (4 cases,
all failing with `prov.statement_collision` before the fix, all passing tier 4 after it).

**Same move: the apv 0.2.0 note.** `vocab/apv-0.2.ttl` kept the 0.1.0 `skos:note` saying the w3id registration was
pending. It now says the namespace is registered (perma-id/w3id.org pull request 6836, merged 2026-10-09), and
`dcterms:modified` is 2026-10-23. The same stale sentence in `vocab/apv-adprov-map-0.1.ttl` is fixed too.
`docs/ns/apv-0.2.ttl` follows (`tools/sync_ns.py`). `docs/ns/apv-0.1.ttl` (published 0.1.0) is unchanged.
`prov/vocab.py` needs no regeneration (`tools/gen_vocab_py.py --check` passes): no term changed. Spec E.4.1 and E.4.6 no
longer call the namespace a placeholder (user-guide finding F-5), and C.4.3 (with C.18 item 6) no longer calls the
`w3id.org` base one. This unblocks the apv 0.2.0 publication to `agentprov-ns` from the main that carries this branch.

**What moves.**
- `prov/engine.py`, `prov/rules/edges.py` and both `vocab/*.ttl` files are in the prov stage's `engine_code_sha256`
  (`stage_scopes.PROV_SEEDS`), so it and the prov `fn_digest` move for every corpus at its next derive or recompute.

  aer engine digest moves (agentdojo `53249fed…` → `b9d06688…`, inspect `9e4ce27e…` → `11402136…`, adprov
  `907b488d…` → `62a3d493…`, wirelog `520b996f…` → `c051cee5…`, openhands `09476c04…` → `2eb6f896…`, and the
  rest), as do sem (agentdojo semantics `18e65983…` → `517fe699…`), prov (`6d9cae35…` → `39c3152c…`) and validation
  (`cea157c5…` → `bdcc94d4…`). The agentdojo adapter digest moves (`5a322774…` → `efc8bbae…`).

  the new catalogue, and no stored corpus holds a provider-`anthropic` session.

  window as item 167 part 1 (the `defence` home), so every family's aer digest moves once for both. Option B (the
  rules in `cap` v2, moving only the agentdojo digests) was rejected: the `defence` home moves them anyway, and A keeps
  the rules where they belong.

**Rebuild-window review round 1 (R1-1..R1-5, the minors and nits; fixes on top of the window, same item).**
- The SSE readers (core `ingest/sse.py` and the harness `parse_sse`) dispatch only what the pinned SDK dispatches: an
  event ended by a single line terminator, or text after the last terminator, is torn, not dispatched; a BOM is kept;
  a per-line bound. Differential tests: 2,000 streams against the SDK algorithm (core), 20,000 against the real
  `SSEDecoder` (backend).
- The stream rebuild is strict and linear (keyed by event name; `message_start` first, ordered indices, typed deltas,
  nothing after `message_stop`); an inconsistent stream is `anthropic_messages.stream_inconsistent` and nothing is
  claimed from it; an incomplete or torn one is `anthropic_messages.stream_incomplete` (rule
  `anthropic_messages.stream_read@1`; catalogue v1 amended in place, cited by nothing yet).
- `redacted_thinking` agrees with the stock dump; a redacted place of a discarded reply is withheld; `sent_form`
  includes the stock chain-of-thought prefix and refuses an unaccounted `system`; a JSON body must be a `Message`.
- Capture redaction refuses an event-stream blob whose joined delta text holds a secret the bytes do not
  (`cap.redact.split`, fail-closed; class 0, the capture distribution).
- The provider-anthropic fixtures join the generic live gates (K.9.1 with the declared thinking exception).
- **Fixture regeneration:** the capture fixtures are regenerated because the window's guarded-sources commit (D-656,
  `a5c8a8ea`) changes the `identity_digests` note's `guarded_sources`, the only projection difference
  (`make_capture_fixtures.py --check` was stale on the window before these fixes): 17 fixtures moved bytes, 16 of them
  with the new identity (round 3 counted them); `autodojo_aborted_kill` had been regenerated with the stale installed
  harness (its kill path runs `-I`) and is regenerated again in round 3 (below).
- **Digest moves of the round-1 fixes** (review round 3, measured): `aer:agentdojo` `edbd908c…` → `6b332eab…`
  (`ingest/sse.py`) and `adapter:agentdojo` `a432f954…` → `6cd1bcef…`; the other 40 digests are unchanged. No stored
  corpus byte moves.

**Rebuild-window review round 3 (R3-1..R3-6; on top of window `1cac458d`, same item).**
- R3-1: an empty text in a discarded reply (Messages: a stream cut after `content_block_start`, an empty delta, a JSON
  empty text block; OpenAI: content `""`) is declared ambiguous as in `_assistant_message`, so mapping no longer aborts

- R3-2: an event-stream body with no `message_start` (garbage, empty, pings only) is inconsistent
  (`no_message_start`): a discarded reply yields no message, `capture_error`.
- R3-3: both fixture generators refuse to run when the installed `agentprov_backend`/`agentprov_capture` differ from
  the checkout's source (the AutoDojo kill path imports the installed copy under `-I`); `autodojo_aborted_kill` is
  regenerated with the source harness (26 guarded sources, 8 `anthropic_llm`). Both `--check` runs are clean after
  `uv sync --offline --reinstall-package agentprov-backend --reinstall-package agentprov-capture`.
- R3-4: a start block's `input_json` no longer seeds a tool input (core and harness), and the event names the SDK
  forwards besides the six make a stream inconsistent (`stream_read@1` amended in place; nothing cites it).
- R3-5: the split-secret scan reads lines at CR/LF/CRLF only (not U+2028/U+2029/U+0085) and joins multi-line
  `data:` (class 0, capture).
